🇳🇵 Nepal–Tibet Border Avalanche & Flood | 26 August 2026 A major ice–rock avalanche near the Nepal–Tibet border triggered a cascading hazard: a large glacier mass collapsed from high elevation, sending ice, rock and sediment into the Lhende Khola. This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. “I Cut Her Body Into Pieces”: Naresh Bhatt Makes Shocking Admission in Mamta Kafle Case What happened to missing Nepali nurse Mamta Kafle Bhatt? Her husband, Naresh Bhatt, has made a shocking admission while testifying in his ongoing murder trial in the United States. On Thursday, November 5, 2026, Bhatt told the court that he found Mamta unconscious on the bedroom floor on July 30, 2024. He claimed that he attempted CPR but believed she was already dead. He further admitted that he used a saw to cut her body into pieces and placed her remains in garbage bags. He said he did this because he panicked and feared being blamed for her death. However, Bhatt denied murdering his wife and claimed that she died by suicide. Prosecutors strongly dispute his account and allege that he killed her before disposing of her remains. Mamta’s body has still not been recovered. The central question before the jury remains: Did Mamta die by suicide, or was she murdered?
